doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: Side-person fees and the Erykah Badu Sorcery sample
summary: He gets fees he asks for; a sampled track from Sorcery earned payment after his lawyer intervened.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: How does it work in this business these days with — do you get payments for things you did over the years, or was it mostly you got a fee? I guess I’m talking about the many things you’ve done as a side person. Do you ever get checks in the mail and wonder what is this for?

Not from doing that. I mean you know I get fees that I suggest or demand that I get. You know you get a 1099 and do that. I mean there’s checks that would be like say Erykah Badu did an album called “Kiss Me on My Neck” and she sampled a track from my, what was it, “Sorcery” album. And she used it on two tracks but they never contacted my lawyer about the copyright of that. So as a result of that, a statutory rate, my lawyer got on there, paid us, paid Dave and I quite a sum over time you know.
